Protect saved archives with one password
The next manual and scheduled backups will be readable without a password. Existing encrypted backups can still be restored with their passwords.
This password protects manual and scheduled backups. It is wrapped by Android Keystore and never stored as plain text.
This archive will be readable without a password. Enable Encryption first if you want to protect it.
This archive is not password-protected. Its contents are readable by anyone who can access the file.
How long backup sets are kept
Choose SMS, calls, or restricted messages
Includes SMS, plus available MMS and RCS records. Restricted messages need the separate option.
Adds hidden messages to the SMS backup; usually end-to-end encrypted RCS messages hidden by Android from non-default SMS apps.
Choose at least one type of record before scheduling automatic backups.

Choose what manual backups include. Restricted messages are usually end-to-end encrypted RCS messages stored in Android’s telephony provider. Android may require Libre SMS Backup to be the default SMS app to read them. Selecting Restricted messages turns off scheduled backups.
Warning: saving this selection turns off scheduled backups because Android restricts these messages for non-default SMS apps.

Android restricts encrypted or otherwise restricted messages for non-default SMS apps, so they are not reliable in background backups. Scheduled backups were turned off. Disable Restricted messages in Backup content before scheduling again.
Your previous schedule settings were restored now that Restricted messages is disabled.
Enable Encryption and set its password first. Scheduled backups reuse that password and never ask for a separate schedule password.

Encryption is optional. Choose Enable encryption to protect future scheduled archives with a password, or continue without it. You can change this later; scheduled backups always use the current Encryption setting.
Choose a day of the month
In shorter months, the backup runs on the last available day.

Open Libre SMS Backup to check the backup settings.
Allow exact alarms so automatic backups can run at the selected time.

Automatic backups may be delayed by battery optimization. Tap to allow reliable background runs.
Choose SMS messages, call logs, or both. Restoring SMS may require Libre SMS Backup to be your default SMS app; existing records are skipped.
Use at least 8 characters. The password is wrapped by Android Keystore and never stored as plain text.
Enter the password used when this backup was created. Leave it empty for an unencrypted archive.
Libre SMS Backup needs read access to SMS and call logs to make a backup. It never sends this data anywhere.

Switch SMS app for this restore

Android requires Libre SMS Backup to be your default SMS app to restore SMS messages. Avoid receiving new MMS messages during this short restore because this app does not deliver incoming MMS. After the restore succeeds, we will ask you to choose your previous default SMS app again.
Libre SMS Backup was not made the default SMS app, so SMS messages were not restored. You can still restore call logs.
Your records were restored successfully. Libre SMS Backup was temporarily made your default SMS app. Choose your previous default SMS app now.
Libre SMS Backup is still the default SMS app. You can switch back from Default apps in Android Settings.

Android only lets the default SMS app read some restricted messages. Libre SMS Backup needs to become your default SMS app temporarily to include them in this backup. Avoid receiving new MMS while it holds that role because incoming MMS delivery is not handled. You can choose your usual SMS app again after the backup.

Libre SMS Backup is a free, open-source Android app for keeping SMS, MMS, and call records under your control. It works locally, optionally protects archives with a password, and has no account, cloud service, tracker, or network permission.
Create an email with optional diagnostics

Would you like to include anonymized technical diagnostics? They contain app and Android details and sanitized error state, but never messages, phone numbers, contacts, passwords, backup files, or storage paths. Your email text is shared only after you choose an app. You can report without diagnostics.
